opener: Lord, I need to tell You the truth instead of performing a peace I don't have: I am exhausted from being hurt by the same person in new ways and calling it fine every time. I smile through the comment that cut. I excuse the silence that followed. I rehearse their side of the story louder than my own just to keep the relationship from collapsing — and somewhere in all that managing, I lost track of how much weight I've quietly agreed to carry. I don't want to hate them. I just don't want to keep shrinking myself to make room for who they refuse to become.
paragraphs: So tonight I'm putting down what was never mine to fix. I will not let their unfinished work become the seat I live in — not the bitterness, not the rehearsed arguments, not the version of me that flinches before it even gets hurt again. Teach me the difference between forgiving someone and staying available to be wounded by them, because I can release the debt without reopening the door.

Grow something in me that doesn't need their apology to be whole — roots deep enough that I can be loved imperfectly by people and still not be moved by what they withhold. Heal the part of me that keeps score, and give me the courage to set the boundary that love, real love, actually requires. In Jesus' name, amen.
